record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Tree support threshold for strong WARM
record.original_question: For finite-graph WARMs with strong reinforcement alpha > 1, the source states that when alpha > 2 every connected component of the limiting support should be a tree. Can the lower bound alpha > 2 be improved, and if so what is the sharp threshold above which every connected component of the surviving-edge support is a tree?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 Improve the lower bound α > 2 for which every connected component is a tree.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite simple connected graph $G = (V, E)$. For each vertex $v \in V$ let $(N_v(t))_{t \geq 0}$ be an independent Poisson process with rate $\lambda_v > 0$. For a reinforcement exponent $\alpha > 1$, the Weakly Reinforced Asymptotically Markovian (WARM) process is defined as follows. Each edge $e \in E$ carries a weight $W_e(t)$ with initial value $W_e(0) = 1$. At every jump time of $N_v$ (a "firing" at $v$), one selects an edge $e$ incident to $v$ with probability proportional to $W_e(t)^{\alpha}$ among edges incident to $v$, and increments $W_e(t)$ by $1$. Let
$$E_\infty = \{ e \in E : W_e(t) \to \infty \text{ as } t \to \infty \}$$
be the (random) set of edges that are reinforced infinitely often, i.e., the surviving-edge support. It is known that for every finite graph and every choice of Poisson rates, if $\alpha > 2$ then almost surely every connected component of the subgraph $(V, E_\infty)$ is a tree (i.e., contains no cycle).

Determine the sharp threshold $\alpha^* \geq 1$ with the following property: for every $\alpha > \alpha^*$, every connected component of $(V, E_\infty)$ is almost surely a tree (for every finite graph $G$ and every choice of positive rates $\{\lambda_v\}$), while for every $\alpha \in (1, \alpha^*)$ there exists a finite graph and a choice of rates such that with positive probability $(V, E_\infty)$ contains a cycle. In particular, can the bound $\alpha^* \leq 2$ be improved?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on WARM in the strong reinforcement regime (e.g., "Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime" and "Absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime") confirm that for sufficiently large α all surviving components are trees of bounded diameter, and that infinitely many phase transitions occur as α↓1. None of the located sources establish a sharp threshold below 2 above which every component is a tree, so the problem of improving the α>2 bound and identifying the sharp value appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: For finite graphs and α>2 all connected components of the surviving-edge subgraph are trees; phase transitions occur as α↓1.
status_evidence.claim: Bound α>2 is the current state of the art; sharp threshold not identified.

status_evidence.title: Absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: For bounded-degree graphs and α sufficiently large depending on degree, surviving edges form only finite components.
status_evidence.claim: Results address very strong reinforcement but do not pin down a sharp tree-threshold below 2.

status_evidence.title: WARM percolation on a regular tree in the strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: For each α>1 there exist regular trees with rates yielding infinite components a.s.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates richness of behavior for 1<α≤2 but does not resolve the cycle-vs-tree threshold.
